checks.note: OAuth2 page lists authorization code, implicit (discouraged), client credentials, bot authorization and webhook flows. The reference page states `Authorization: Bot/Bearer/Basic` headers, with Basic applying only to OAuth2 token endpoints. OAuth2 is real API access for third-party apps, not just login. The bot-token header comes from the reference page, not the OAuth2 page.

The OAuth2 page mentions neither free account creation nor cost or app review. It does confirm the partner-only scopes (applications.builds.upload, dm_channels.read, identify.premium, rpc*, voice), the relationships.read form, and a Verified bots mention with no details. The free self-serve claim is plausible but is not stated on a fetched page.
The reference page describes an HTTP REST API and a Gateway WebSocket API. The breadth rating of broad is a judgment call that the page does not contradict.

A search result points to docs.discord.com/mcp, described as an official docs-search/read-only filesystem MCP. A direct fetch returned HTTP 405 (consistent with an MCP endpoint but not a confirmation). I could not verify vendor ownership. Even if official, it only searches the docs and does not operate Discord. The community discord-mcp repos appear in third-party listings but I did not fetch the repo. The best-supported classification is community for agent actions.

ready_with_caveats is consistent with the verified facts. The caveats are: bots only work in guilds they are installed in, some scopes are partner-gated, the DiscordBot User-Agent is required, and the rate-limit revocation statement is on the reference page.

corrected.one_liner: Discord is a chat, voice and community platform organized into servers (guilds) and channels, with a developer platform for bots and apps.
corrected.auth_notes: Bot token sent as `Authorization: Bot <token>` (from app settings; a static credential). OAuth2 for user-delegated access: authorization code (with PKCE), implicit (not recommended), client credentials (bearer for bot owner), bot authorization flow, and webhook flow. Access tokens are sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Basic auth (client_id:client_secret) applies only to the OAuth2 token endpoints. Incoming webhooks are an additional URL-based mechanism.
corrected.access_notes: Anyone with a free Discord account can create an application and bot in the developer portal. This is inferred and not stated on a fetched page; the OAuth2 and reference pages mention neither cost nor app review. Some scopes need partner approval: dm_channels.read, rpc*, voice, identify.premium and applications.builds.upload. relationships.read needs an access request via the Social SDK form. Verified-bot status is referenced for growing past the guild cap, but the docs page doesn't state the cap number or the criteria.
corrected.blocker: Bot actions work only in guilds where the bot is installed, and the user must add it. User-token actions are limited by OAuth scopes. Some scopes (DM channel reads, RPC, voice) are partner-only. Rate limits apply, and the docs say API users who regularly ignore them will have their API keys revoked. Bots must send a DiscordBot User-Agent. A docs.discord.com/mcp endpoint appears to be a docs-search-only MCP (not confirmed; it returned HTTP 405 to a plain GET) and does not operate Discord, so MCP for actions is classed as community.
